deviations: IQR regressions (one observation per property, IQR pooled across all of the property's surveyed workers): survey-round FE uses the survey year of each property's first row in the file, since the paper does not say how a round is assigned when a property's workers span several rounds.
All survey years in the data file (2000-2013) are kept, although the paper's text says 2002-2013; the file contains no 2002/2003 rounds, and no year restriction was applied.
Former-owner clusters are identified by Expropretario_ISTA; bandwidth samples are |own_amt - 500| <= bw (uniform kernel); percentiles use R quantile type 2 (Stata pctile convention).
notes: Two exploratory runs (attempt-1: variable listing; attempt-2: identifiers, bandwidth sample sizes, years per property), with no RESULT lines. Specification: hh_income_pc ~ Above500 + norm_dist + Above500:norm_dist | year (linear in the running variable on each side of the cutoff), with SEs clustered by former owner (Expropretario_ISTA), on worker-level data within 300/150 ha. IQR: 75th minus 25th percentile of hh_income_pc per property (match_id) among properties with >=5 surveyed workers, one row per property, with the same RD regression. Attempt-3 was the first scored run. Its coefficients are identical to the final run's, but fixest's default dropped singleton survey-year FE groups in the IQR regressions (N 75/26). The final run keeps singletons (fixef.rm='none'), as Stata's reg with i.year would, giving N 76/28. The change was made for that methodological reason only; no comparison with paper values was made. Cluster counts reported are those of the worker-level samples (columns 1/2); the IQR samples have fewer owners (71 at 300 ha, 25 at 150 ha; printed as DIAG). While reading the paper's methods prose, the results paragraph introducing Table 5 came into view; it mentions a dollar figure for the IQR difference. It was not used for, and did not influence, any specification choice.
